projects.title: Hydrogen-generation prototype
projects.role: Designed, built and tested it myself
projects.summary: A steel-plate hydrogen-generation system, taken from first concept through construction to practical tests of its gas output.
projects.outcome: A working prototype, tested for gas output.

image.alt: Line illustration of two steel plates in water with gas bubbles rising

detail.problem: A hands-on side project: could a simple design built around steel plates generate hydrogen gas, and what does it take to get from a concept on paper to a device that actually works?
detail.approach: I worked from concept to construction: designing a system around steel plates, building it, and then testing in practice how much gas it produced.
detail.contribution: All of it: the design, the build and the testing.
detail.outcome: A working prototype that produced gas in practical tests.

projects.title: GPT-based research assistant
projects.summary: An assistant that finds start-ups and organises their contact details by country and city, to speed up market and partner research.

image.alt: Line illustration of a magnifying glass over a map with marked cities

detail.problem: Finding start-ups in a market and collecting their contact details by hand is slow, and the results end up scattered and hard to use for outreach.
detail.approach: A GPT-based workflow that identifies start-ups and structures their contact information by country and city, so the results can be used directly for outreach and partner research.
detail.contribution: I designed the workflow and built the assistant.
detail.outcome: A working assistant that returns start-ups with their contact details grouped by country and city, ready for outreach and partner research.

projects.title: Zon op Haarlemmermeer
projects.role: Team member, with an equal share of the analysis and strategy work
projects.summary: A citizen energy cooperative had sold 20% of the shares in a roughly 400-panel solar roof, and needed 70% before it could be built. We worked out why, and how to close the gap.

image.alt: Line illustration of solar panels on a municipal roof under the sun

detail.problem: Zon op Haarlemmermeer, a young energy cooperative run by and for citizens, planned a solar roof of roughly 400 panels on a municipal building, supported by the national SCE subsidy. Only 20% of the shares had been sold, and 70% were needed before construction could go ahead.
detail.approach: For the course Marketing Sustainable Innovations at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, our team analysed the barriers to share sales, mapped the stakeholders and built a value-exchange model. From that we proposed a marketing campaign, a strategy for creating buy-in, and a co-creation plan.
detail.contribution: I shared the research, analysis and recommendations equally with my teammates.
detail.outcome: We delivered the analysis and our recommendations, a marketing campaign, a buy-in strategy and a co-creation plan, as a written case report for the course.

projects.title: From Linear to Circular
projects.role: Author, written with Duisburg Business & Innovation GmbH
projects.summary: How policy, institutions, incentives and cooperation shape the move from linear to circular production in post-industrial Duisburg, compared with Amsterdam and Singapore.

image.alt: Line illustration of a linear arrow bending into a closed loop around an industrial skyline

detail.problem: Full title: From Linear to Circular: Policy Pathways for Economic Resilience and Sustainability in Duisburg's Post-Industrial Transition. The question was what shapes the shift from linear to circular production in a post-industrial city.
detail.approach: A policy and institutional analysis of Duisburg, looking at policy, institutions, incentives and cooperation, with Amsterdam and Singapore as comparative cases. Written alongside my work as a project assistant at Duisburg Business & Innovation GmbH.
detail.outcome: Part of my completed M.A. in Philosophy, Politics & Economics at Witten/Herdecke University.

projects.title: This website
projects.summary: My personal site, written as plain HTML and hosted free on GitHub Pages, with structured data for search engines and AI assistants and cookieless visitor statistics.
projects.outcome: Live at momohammadi.nl, verified in Google Search Console and imported into Bing.

image.alt: Screenshot of the opening screen of momohammadi.nl

detail.problem: I wanted one place that explains my mix of engineering, economics and policy better than a CV can, and that people and search engines can actually find.
detail.approach: A single static page without a framework, hosted on GitHub Pages under my own domain. Structured data (JSON-LD), a sitemap and an llms.txt file help search engines and AI assistants understand it. GoatCounter counts visits without cookies.
detail.contribution: Design, writing and build, working with AI coding tools.
detail.outcome: Live at momohammadi.nl, verified in Google Search Console and imported into Bing Webmaster Tools.

projects.title: Meetout
projects.role: Product owner: defined the product, its rules and safety features, and built it with AI coding tools
projects.summary: An app for meeting new people around Oss through small public hangouts: post a plan, others ask to join, the group chats and meets. References after each meetup build trust.

image.alt: Line illustration of map pins connected by a dotted path with chat bubbles

detail.problem: Meeting new people in a smaller town like Oss is hard once you are past school or university. There are few easy, low-pressure ways to join a few others for something small nearby.
detail.approach: A mobile-first web app with an Android version. Someone posts a hangout at a public spot, others ask to join, and the host accepts or declines. The group chats live, and after meeting up people leave references with descriptive tags. Safety is built in: an 18+ check, public meeting spots, and negative tags that only the person concerned can see. The launch version runs on Firebase with phone sign-in and data stored in the Netherlands.
detail.contribution: I defined the product, its rules and safety features, and built it with AI coding tools.
detail.outcome: In development. The launch version runs on Firebase and is not public yet.

projects.title: Dogout
projects.role: Product owner, adapting the Meetout codebase to a new audience
projects.summary: Dog play dates in Noord-Brabant, starting in Oss. Owners make a profile for their dog, get matched with dogs of similar energy, size and play style, and plan open or private play dates.

image.alt: Line illustration of paw prints and a ball along a dotted path

detail.problem: Finding good play partners for a dog is hit and miss. Dogs differ a lot in energy, size and play style, and a poor match makes a play date stressful for dogs and owners.
detail.approach: Built from a copy of Meetout: a React and TypeScript web app in Dutch and English on Firebase, with an Android version. Matching uses each dog's energy, size and play style, and a Hangout view shows which dogs are out nearby right now.
detail.contribution: I defined the product and adapted the Meetout codebase for it, working with AI coding tools.
detail.outcome: In development and not public yet.

projects.title: Tend
projects.role: Product owner, working with a team of AI role agents
projects.summary: A no-shame life game for adults with ADHD, informed by CBT techniques: small real-life steps help your avatar grow, and missing a day never costs you anything.

image.alt: Line illustration of a small sprout character inside a rounded frame with checked steps

detail.problem: Many habit apps punish a missed day with a lost streak. For adults with ADHD that often turns a tool meant to help into one more source of shame.
detail.approach: A playtest prototype that runs in the browser with no accounts. The game rules are written as tested functions. The project is run like a small company, with AI agents in roles from product and design to privacy, marketing and finance, each following written rules. Tend is a self-help game, not a treatment.
detail.contribution: I set the direction and decisions as product owner and coordinate the AI role agents.
detail.outcome: A playable browser prototype for playtesting. It has not been released publicly.

projects.title: AI workflow automation
projects.summary: Python pipelines that check online sources on a schedule, score new items with AI, draft tailored documents and wait for a human approval before anything is sent.

image.alt: Line illustration of connected workflow steps ending in a hand-drawn approval tick

detail.problem: Checking many online sources by hand and writing a tailored document for every relevant new item is repetitive work that is easy to fall behind on.
detail.approach: Scheduled Python pipelines that check sources, filter and score new items with AI, and draft tailored documents. Nothing is sent without a one-tap human approval. A separate review loop has two AI models check each other's work, backed by automated regression tests and an audit of every command run.
detail.contribution: I designed and built the pipelines and the review loop.
detail.outcome: In personal use. Every outgoing document still needs a human approval before it is sent.
